title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous pages. We have a smooth S over T and a morphism of O_S-modules u: E' -> E with cokernel E''. Presumably the sequence 0 -> E' -> E -> E'' -> 0 is exact, and E' sits inside the horizontal part. E carries a connection d^0_E: E -> E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} relative to T, with next differential d^1_E. P' is a torsor (sheaf-theoretic) under E', and P = P' ×^{E'} E is the pushed-out E-torsor. Integrable connections on P correspond to maps d_{P'}: P' -> E⊗Ω^1 that are affine over d^0_E∘u, i.e. d_{P'}(x'+ξ') = d_{P'}(x') + d^0_E(u ξ'), and land in the cocycles (d^1_E∘d_{P'} = 0). This is (43)-(44).

This page. Take a differential operator Δ: E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} -> F that kills d^0_E∘u, as an operator: Δ∘d^0_E∘u = 0. Locally d_{P'} gives a section of E⊗Ω^1 that is well defined modulo d^0_E(u(ξ')). So Δ(d_{P'}(x')) does not depend on x', and the local values glue to a global section ν_Δ(P', d_{P'}) ∈ Γ(S,F). This is (46). It is an 'inhomogeneous Picard–Fuchs value' attached to the torsor with connection.

The universal case is F = P^∞_{S/T}(E⊗Ω^1)/Im P^∞_{S/T}(E'), where P^∞ denotes the sheaf of infinite principal parts (jets). The map is the jet prolongation of the first-order operator d^0_E∘u: E' -> E -> E⊗Ω^1. Any Δ then factors uniquely through this universal quotient.

Comparison with the earlier construction μ_D. μ_D is the 'Gauss–Manin section' of F attached to a Picard–Fuchs operator D: E'' -> F and data (P,σ), where E carries a stratification. Assume E has a stratification and d^0_E is the connection deduced from it. To each Δ associate D_0 = Δ∘d^0_E: E -> F (47). D_0 vanishes on E' by hypothesis, so it descends to D: E'' -> F, which is a Picard–Fuchs operator in the sense of (30). The claim is ν_Δ = μ_D (48). This reduces the stratification-based invariant μ_D to the connection-based invariant ν_Δ. The margin says 'faire la vérification': the check was not carried out.

The next page completes the reduction. In characteristic 0 with Ω^1 flat, every D on affine S comes from some Δ. The reason given is a lemma: operators killing the horizontal jets are exactly those of the form Δ∘d^0_E, unique up to Δ'∘d^1_E. This is a Spencer/de Rham-type exactness statement.

The mathematical purpose is a sheaf/torsor-theoretic formalism for applying Picard–Fuchs operators to non-horizontal objects: torsors, or extensions of a module with connection by a horizontal one. The output is a section of F. This is exactly the shape of the Manin map (Manin's 'theorem of the kernel': a section of an abelian scheme gives an extension of D-modules, and a Picard–Fuchs operator annihilating periods sends it to a function), and of inhomogeneous Picard–Fuchs equations for normal functions.
errors: The identity (48) ν_Δ = μ_D is asserted without proof; Grothendieck's own margin says 'faire la vérification'. It is plausible by unwinding definitions, but sign and normalisation conventions (how σ and the stratification enter μ_D) are not checked on the page.

'Δ nul sur d^0_E(u(E'))' must be read as an identity of differential operators (Δ∘d^0_E∘u = 0), not merely vanishing on sections. Otherwise the universal F via P^∞ would not be correct. The page's formulation is slightly loose.

ν_Δ is first obtained locally (d_{P'} gives a section only locally, as the previous page notes 'loc.!'). Gluing is fine because the value is independent of choices, but F should be a sheaf. The previous page speaks of a presheaf quotient P^∞(E'')/u Sol(E'), so sheafification may be needed.

ideas.what: Attaching to a torsor P' under a horizontal submodule E', with a compatible integrable connection on P = P'×^{E'}E, a global section ν_Δ ∈ Γ(S,F) by applying a differential operator Δ that kills d^0_E∘u
ideas.modern_name: Manin map / inhomogeneous Picard–Fuchs value of an extension of D-modules (normal function)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Yu. Manin (1963, function-field Mordell; 'theorem of the kernel'); later reformulations by Coleman (1990), Chai (1991), Bertrand, Buium
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA/SGA; only these unpublished Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs notes, as far as known

ideas.what: Universal target F = P^∞(E⊗Ω^1)/Im P^∞(E') representing differential operators Δ with Δ∘d^0_E∘u = 0
ideas.modern_name: Representing differential operators via sheaves of principal parts (jets)
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16.8 (principal parts, differential operators), applied here to a specific quotient

ideas.what: Comparing the connection-based invariant ν_Δ with the stratification-based Gauss–Manin section μ_D via D = (Δ∘d^0_E) descended to E''
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of Manin map computed via connection vs via stratification / Picard–Fuchs operator on the quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (implicit in Manin, Katz 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations', Chai)

ideas.what: Lemma (next page): in char 0 with Ω flat, operators killing horizontal jets are exactly Δ∘d^0_E, with indeterminacy Δ'∘d^1_E
ideas.modern_name: Exactness of the jet/Spencer form of the de Rham complex for a module with integrable connection

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in torsor/jet language over a general base S/T with stratifications, the invariant obtained by applying a Picard–Fuchs operator to a torsor (extension) under a horizontal submodule. This is essentially a general, characteristic-free framework for the Manin map. He also notes a comparison between the connection version and the stratification version, which is relevant in positive characteristic, where the two differ. The literature (Coleman, Chai, Buium, Bertrand–Pillay) treats the Manin map mostly in char 0 via D-modules or differential algebra, and does not credit Grothendieck with this formalism.
missed.quote: on voit que Δ définit une section (46) ν_Δ(P', d_{P'}) ∈ Γ(S, F) ... on trouve que (48) ν_Δ = μ_D, ce qui donne la réduction annoncée.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A stratification-based (char-p / crystalline) version of the Manin map is of interest for function-field Mordell–Lang in positive characteristic and for p-adic/differential-arithmetic analogues (Buium's δ-characters). These notes sketch such a framework early (c.1972).

missed.claim: The key comparison ν_Δ = μ_D was left unverified ('faire la vérification'). The positive-characteristic case, where not every D comes from a Δ (the lemma needs char 0), is not treated.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In char p the gap between μ_D and ν_Δ measures the difference between stratifications and connections, i.e. a p-curvature/Cartier-type phenomenon. This links to the Cartier operation in the same dossier.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but largely formal construction. Its notable aspect is that it amounts to an early general torsor/jet formalism for the Manin map (with a stratification-vs-connection comparison) that is not in Grothendieck's published work. The underlying idea, however, is known through Manin and later authors.
transcription_corrections: 'prenons d^0_E divisé d'icelle' should likely read 'prenons d^0_E déduit d'icelle' (the connection deduced from the stratification).
The superscript 'd^0_E∘u' above a V-shaped mark is an annotation labelling the composite E' -> E -> E⊗Ω^1, not part of the formula.
'puisque par hypothèse Δ [?] sur E'' should read roughly 'puisque par hypothèse Δ∘d^0_E est nulle sur E'' (interlinear insertion '{Δ∘d^0_E est nulle}').
The margin note at (48) reads 'faire la vérification'.
